title: Government Forms Automation with AI: Fast & Flexible Tools in 2026
summary: Start with a government form template, build a workflow in plain English, and connect Skyvern to the tools your team already uses.
body_markdown:
Here's my guess: you're not researching government forms automation out of curiosity. Somewhere on your desk is a renewal, a registration, or a weekly filing that eats hours it shouldn't, on a portal that logs you out mid-form.


I built Skyvern to fix this. It's an[AI browser agent](https://www.skyvern.com/products) that reads any form the way a person does, fills it from your data, handles the login and 2FA, and saves the confirmation.


This guide covers how to setup government forms automation and which forms to automate first. Then it walks through the setup steps and the practices that keep filings safe.


## How to Automate Government Forms with AI


Government forms automation uses software to fill out, submit, and track forms for taxes, permits, licenses, and business registrations. It reduces repetitive data entry for your team.


Traditional scripts can do this, but they can break when a website changes or logs you out. AI browser agents like Skyvern can read the page, log in, and[fill forms using your data](https://www.skyvern.com/blog/automate-form-filling-with-skyvern-ai-browser-automation/) . They can adapt to layout changes, and you can set up the workflow to ask a person for help when needed.


Here’s how to set it up.


### Step 1: Collect the Data


Application forms are really just lists of questions, so start by collecting the answers and data in one place.


You can put the application data straight into the workflow. Or point the AI agent at a public page like a Google Doc with your company details.


You can also give all information as an input to the workflow.


### Step 2: Log In and Set Up 2FA


Next, logins. Different kinds of automation apps handle this differently. But essentially, you log in once in the agent's browser, and it saves the cookies for the next run.


Set up the[multi factor authentication](https://www.skyvern.com/blog/how-skyvern-handles-authentication/) the same way, with TOTP or email codes going to the agent instead of your phone.


Skyvern handles it in such a way that credentials never reach the model. So sensitive information is always out of prompts.


And if you're worried about data privacy, Skyvern is open source, so you can[run all of this locally](https://www.skyvern.com/developers) on your own machine and use your own LLMs.


### Step 3: Build the Workflow (and Give It Context)


Describe the form to be filled in plain English adding all the context and instructions. Include:


- What to do when an unexpected error appears.
- What to do with a field it has never seen.


Skyvern's built-in email tool can escalate to a human when the AI encounters errors or gets confused.


Add data validation rules for the formats the agency's digital forms enforce.


Spell out the conditional logic: eligibility criteria, additional forms that follow an approval, which supporting documents to upload.


Tell it what the data extraction should return too, like the confirmation number as JSON. The more context the agent has, the fewer surprises you get.


### Step 4: Watch the First Run


Do the first run live and watch the agent submit forms to government agencies in front of you.


Skyvern streams the agent's browser, and if it gets stuck, you can hit Take Over, drive the browser yourself, and then hand control back.


You can use this to bring in a human for payments, e-signatures and sworn certifications.


### Step 5: Save It as a Workflow


Once a run completes, save it as a template workflow.


Now it becomes one of your automated workflows. You can set it up to run on a trigger schedule, or across different datasets.


If you're building apps on top of this, use webhooks to push real time status and confirmations.


### Step 6: Save the Run Records


Set up a system to record everything: confirmation receipts, downloaded artifacts, screen recordings.


Future you needs them for audits and compliance requirements, and debugging a failed filing is far easier with a replay. Skyvern does it automatically.


You can also use this to calculate the time and cost savings per filing, error reduction and improved efficiency.


## Common Government Forms and Workflows for Skyvern Users


If you’re using Skyvern for government paperwork, these common workflows are useful starting points. The links go to official forms, filing services, and lookup tools. State and local requirements vary; the California and New York City links are examples.


Workflow Official forms and portals Typical task


Business and employer registration[IRS Form SS-4](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-ss-4?ref=skyvern.com) ;[California EDD DE-1](https://edd.ca.gov/siteassets/files/pdf_pub_ctr/de1.pdf?ref=skyvern.com) Apply for an EIN or register a California employer payroll tax account.


Federal payroll taxes[Form 941](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-941?ref=skyvern.com) ;[Form 940](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-940?ref=skyvern.com) Report quarterly payroll taxes and annual federal unemployment taxes.


Tax representation[Form 2848](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-2848?ref=skyvern.com) Authorize a representative to act before the IRS.


Employee wage reporting[SSA Forms W-2 and W-3](https://www.ssa.gov/employer/W2checklist.htm?ref=skyvern.com) Report employee wages and the employer’s wage totals.


Certified payroll and injury reporting[DOL Form WH-347](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/forms/wh347?ref=skyvern.com) ;[OSHA Form 300A](https://www.osha.gov/recordkeeping/forms?ref=skyvern.com) Prepare weekly certified payroll reports or annual workplace injury and illness summaries.


Employment eligibility[Form I-9](https://www.uscis.gov/sites/default/files/document/forms/i-9.pdf?ref=skyvern.com) ;[E-Verify](https://www.e-verify.gov/?ref=skyvern.com) Prepare and retain I-9 records; run employment eligibility checks through E-Verify.


Medicare enrollment[CMS enrollment forms and PECOS](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/enrollment-renewal/providers-suppliers?ref=skyvern.com) Enroll or revalidate providers and suppliers using the applicable CMS-855 application or PECOS.


[Medicaid applications](https://www.skyvern.com/blog/medicaid-enrollment-automation/)[State Medicaid application links](https://www.medicaid.gov/about-us/where-can-people-get-help-medicaid-chip?ref=skyvern.com) Apply for patient coverage through the relevant state agency.


Healthcare exclusion screening[HHS-OIG exclusions search](https://exclusions.oig.hhs.gov/Default.aspx?ref=skyvern.com) Check individuals and organizations against the federal exclusions list.


Motor carrier registration[FMCSA Form MCS-150](https://www.fmcsa.dot.gov/registration/form-mcs-150-and-instructions-motor-carrier-identification-report?ref=skyvern.com) ;[UCR registration](https://ucr.gov/?ref=skyvern.com) Update a USDOT record or renew Unified Carrier Registration.


Federal contracting[SAM.gov registration](https://sam.gov/entity-registration?ref=skyvern.com) ;[entity search](https://sam.gov/entity-information?ref=skyvern.com) Register or renew an entity for federal awards, or look up entity records.


State payroll and sales tax filings[California EDD e-Services](https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/e-services_for_business?ref=skyvern.com) ;[CDTFA returns](https://cdtfa.ca.gov/services/file-a-return.htm?ref=skyvern.com) File state payroll or sales and use tax returns.


Business entity filings and checks[California Statements of Information](https://www.sos.ca.gov/business-programs/bizfile?ref=skyvern.com) ;[Delaware entity search](https://icis.corp.delaware.gov/eCorp/EntitySearch/NameSearch.aspx?ref=skyvern.com) Update business records or check entity details. Delaware restricts automated searches.


Local permits and business licenses[NYC DOB NOW](https://a810-dobnow.nyc.gov/?ref=skyvern.com) ;[NYC business licenses](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dca/businesses/licenses.page?ref=skyvern.com) Apply for[building permits](https://www.skyvern.com/blog/automate-construction-permit-applications/) , manage inspections, or apply for and renew business licenses.


Court filings[Federal court CM/ECF](https://www.uscourts.gov/court-records/electronic-filing-cm-ecf?ref=skyvern.com) Submit case documents through the relevant court’s electronic filing system.


Public records requests[FOIA.gov](https://www.foia.gov/?ref=skyvern.com) Request records from federal agencies; state and local requests use separate portals.


Related credential checks include[ASHA certification verification](https://www.asha.org/certification/cert-verify/?ref=skyvern.com) and the[BACB certification registry](https://www.bacb.com/verify-certification/?ref=skyvern.com) . These verify professional certification rather than government licenses.
